questions.q: True or false? In two-three-three, our central midfielder starts as an extra defender.
questions.explain: Right, it's false. The central midfielder starts ahead in midfield and drops only when needed.
choiceExplanations: The shape starts with just two defenders. The central midfielder plays ahead until the middle needs cover.
Right, it's false. The central midfielder starts ahead in midfield and drops only when needed.

questions.q: Put the central midfielder's jobs in order, from first to last.
options: Central midfielder drops between the backs
Blue passes back, two forwards stay
questions.explain: Yes. Three high forwards pull the midfielder back, and two high forwards let them rejoin midfield.
choiceExplanations: Yes. Three high forwards pull the midfielder back, and two high forwards let them rejoin midfield.
The midfielder drops only after spotting three high forwards against our two backs.
Blue passes back after our midfielder has already dropped to cover the middle.
Rejoining comes last, once only two forwards stay high for our two backs.

questions.q: Blue attacks our right, so our right back goes wide. Where does the central midfielder go?
options: Beside the ball with the right back
The middle, between our two backs
questions.explain: Yes. The backs take the wide forwards, so the midfielder covers Blue's striker in the middle.
choiceExplanations: Two of us at the ball leaves Blue's striker free in the middle.
Blue has three high forwards and we have two backs. The middle striker is unmarked.
